title: Die zwölf Apostel
source: Brüder Grimm, Kinder- und Hausmärchen, Band 2, 7. Auflage (Ausgabe letzter Hand), Dieterich, Göttingen 1857, KHM 202. Text from Wikisource („Die zwölf Apostel (1857)“, twice proofread against the original). Fresh translation made directly from the German; 1857 spelling preserved exactly.
about: The first of the ten Kinderlegenden appended to the 1857 edition: three hundred years before Christ's birth, a destitute mother sends her twelve sons out into the world to find bread. Each is met in turn by a shining child who leads him to a rock cave with twelve cradles, where all twelve fall asleep for three hundred years — until they wake on the night of Christ's birth as the twelve apostles.

sentences.t: Es war dreihundert Jahre vor des Herrn Christi Geburt, da lebte eine Mutter, die hatte zwölf Söhne, war aber so arm und dürftig, daß sie nicht wußte womit sie ihnen länger das Leben erhalten sollte.
sentences.l: It was three hundred years before the Lord Christ’s birth; there lived a mother who had twelve sons, but was so poor and needy that she did not know with what she could keep them alive any longer.
sentences.i: Three hundred years before the birth of Christ the Lord, there lived a mother who had twelve sons, but was so poor and destitute she no longer knew how she could keep them alive.
sentences.n: “Christi Geburt” — birth of Christ; “Christi” is the Latin genitive of Christus, kept in German for the sacred name (as in “vor Christi Geburt”). The verb “erhalten” here is “sustain, keep alive,” not “receive.” “Womit” = with what, by what means.

sentences.t: Sie betete täglich zu Gott, er möchte doch geben daß alle ihre Söhne mit dem verheißenen Heiland auf Erden zusammen wären.
sentences.l: She prayed daily to God that he might grant that all her sons might be on earth together with the promised Saviour.
sentences.i: She prayed to God every day that he might grant that all her sons might live on earth together with the promised Saviour.
sentences.n: “Möchte … geben daß …” is a reported wish, subjunctive: “that he might grant.” “der verheißene Heiland” — the promised Saviour, i.e. Christ; the tale reaches back to the time before the Nativity. “auf Erden” = on earth (archaic dative singular of Erde, still standard in devotional German).

sentences.t: Als nun ihre Noth immer größer ward, schickte sie einen nach dem andern in die Welt, um sich ihr Brot zu suchen.
sentences.l: As now their need grew ever greater, she sent them one after the other out into the world to seek their bread.
sentences.i: As their need grew ever greater, she sent them one after another out into the world to seek their bread.
sentences.n: “ward” = wurde (became; the older past of werden). “Noth” = Not (1857 spelling of Not, need, hardship). “sich sein Brot suchen” — to seek one’s bread, i.e. to earn one’s keep.

sentences.t: Der älteste hieß Petrus, der gieng aus, und war schon weit gegangen, eine ganze Tagreise, da gerieth er in einen großen Wald.
sentences.l: The eldest was called Peter; he set out, and had already gone far, a whole day’s journey, when he came into a great forest.
sentences.i: The eldest was called Peter; he set out and had already travelled a good way — a whole day’s journey — when he found himself in a great forest.
sentences.n: “gieng” and “gerieth” are 1857 spellings of ging and geriet. “eine Tagreise” — a day’s journey, a common medieval measure of distance. “geraten in” = to end up in, to find oneself in (usually unintentionally).

sentences.t: Er suchte einen Ausweg, konnte aber keinen finden und verirrte sich immer tiefer; dabei empfand er so großen Hunger daß er sich kaum aufrecht erhalten konnte.
sentences.l: He looked for a way out, but could find none, and strayed ever deeper; meanwhile he felt so great a hunger that he could scarcely hold himself upright.
sentences.i: He looked for a way out but could find none, and strayed deeper and deeper; and with it he felt such hunger that he could scarcely stand.
sentences.n: “sich verirren” — to lose one’s way, a reflexive. “sich aufrecht erhalten” — to keep oneself upright; here erhalten is again “sustain, keep,” not “receive.”

sentences.t: Endlich ward er so schwach, daß er liegen bleiben mußte und glaubte dem Tode nahe zu sein.
sentences.l: At last he grew so weak that he had to lie where he was and believed himself to be near to death.
sentences.i: At last he grew so weak he had to lie down where he was and thought himself close to death.
sentences.n: “liegen bleiben” — to remain lying, i.e. to be unable to get up again. “dem Tode nahe” takes the dative (nahe governs the dative); “Tode” is the older dative singular of Tod.

sentences.t: Da stand auf einmal neben ihm ein kleiner Knabe, der glänzte und war so schön und freundlich wie ein Engel.
sentences.l: Then all at once there stood beside him a small boy, who shone and was as beautiful and kindly as an angel.
sentences.i: Then all at once a small boy was standing beside him, who shone and was as beautiful and kindly as an angel.
sentences.n: “auf einmal” = all at once, suddenly. “Knabe” — boy, lad (an older word; today Junge is usual).

sentences.t: Das Kind schlug seine Händchen zusammen daß er aufschauen und es anblicken mußte.
sentences.l: The child clapped its little hands together, so that he had to look up and gaze at it.
sentences.i: The child clapped its little hands together, so that Peter had to look up and gaze at it.
sentences.n: “Händchen” — little hands (diminutive of Hände). “aufschauen” is separable — “to look up”; here it appears in an infinitive after mußte, so the particle stays attached. The daß-clause here reads as “so that,” a common consecutive use without a comma before it in 1857 punctuation.

sentences.t: Da sprach es „warum sitzest du da so betrübt?“
sentences.l: Then it said, “Why do you sit there so grieved?”
sentences.n: “Sitzest” is the older 2nd sg. of sitzen (modern sitzt). “Es” is neuter because Kind is neuter, though the child will be revealed as an angel. Grimm punctuates direct speech with German double quotation marks and no comma before the quote — reproduced in t exactly.

sentences.t: „Ach,“ antwortete Petrus, „ich gehe umher in der Welt und suche mein Brot, damit ich noch den verheißenen lieben Heiland sehe; das ist mein größter Wunsch.“
sentences.l: “Alas,” answered Peter, “I go about in the world and seek my bread, so that I may yet see the promised dear Saviour; that is my greatest wish.”
sentences.i: “Alas,” answered Peter, “I go about the world seeking my bread, so that I may still see the promised, dear Saviour; that is my greatest wish.”
sentences.n: “damit” + subjunctive introduces a purpose clause: “so that I may.” “noch” here = “still, yet” — he hopes to live to see the Saviour.

sentences.t: Das Kind sprach „komm mit, so soll dein Wunsch erfüllt werden.“
sentences.l: The child said, “Come with [me], and so shall your wish be fulfilled.”
sentences.i: The child said, “Come with me, and your wish shall be fulfilled.”
sentences.n: “komm mit” — the particle mit implies “with me”; German leaves it out where English needs it. Square brackets in l supply the elided pronoun. “so soll” — “and then/thus shall”; the so links the condition to the consequence.

sentences.t: Es nahm den armen Petrus an der Hand und führte ihn zwischen Felsen zu einer großen Höhle.
sentences.l: It took poor Peter by the hand and led him among rocks to a great cave.
sentences.i: It took poor Peter by the hand and led him among the rocks to a great cave.
sentences.n: “an der Hand nehmen” — literally “to take by the hand” (dative of place), an idiom preserved word for word in English.

sentences.t: Wie sie hineinkamen, so blitzte alles von Gold Silber und Krystall, und in der Mitte standen zwölf Wiegen neben einander.
sentences.l: As they came in, everything flashed with gold, silver and crystal, and in the middle stood twelve cradles side by side.
sentences.i: As they came in, everything flashed with gold, silver and crystal, and in the middle twelve cradles stood side by side.
sentences.n: “Wie … so” is a paired conjunction here — “when …, then …”. “Krystall” = Kristall (1857 spelling). The absence of commas between “Gold Silber und Krystall” is Grimm’s; reproduced in t as printed.

sentences.t: Da sprach das Englein „lege dich in die erste und schlaf ein wenig, ich will dich wiegen.“
sentences.l: Then the little angel said, “Lay yourself in the first one and sleep a little, I will rock you.”
sentences.i: Then the little angel said, “Lie down in the first one and sleep a little; I will rock you.”
sentences.n: “Englein” — little angel (diminutive of Engel). “wiegen” — to rock (a cradle); the same verb gives the noun Wiege (cradle). “sich legen” — reflexive, to lay oneself down, i.e. to lie down.

sentences.t: Das that Petrus, und das Englein sang ihm und wiegte ihn so lange bis er eingeschlafen war.
sentences.l: That Peter did, and the little angel sang to him and rocked him so long until he had fallen asleep.
sentences.i: Peter did so, and the little angel sang to him and rocked him until he had fallen asleep.
sentences.n: “that” = tat (1857 spelling of tat, from thun/tun). “so lange bis” — “as long until,” i.e. until (the so lange emphasises duration). “einschlafen” — to fall asleep (separable ein-).

sentences.t: Und wie er schlief, kam der zweite Bruder, den auch sein Schutzenglein herein führte, und ward wie der erste in den Schlaf gewiegt, und so kamen die andern nach der Reihe, bis alle zwölfe da lagen in den goldenen Wiegen und schliefen.
sentences.l: And as he slept, there came the second brother, whom his guardian angel also led in, and he was rocked into sleep like the first, and so the others came in turn, until all twelve lay there in the golden cradles and slept.
sentences.i: And as he slept, the second brother came in, led by his guardian angel too, and was rocked to sleep like the first; and so the others came one after another, until all twelve lay in the golden cradles asleep.
sentences.n: “Schutzenglein” — little guardian angel (diminutive of Schutzengel). “in den Schlaf gewiegt” — rocked into sleep, passive. “nach der Reihe” = in order, one after another. “zwölfe” is an inflected form of zwölf, used substantively — “all twelve of them.”

sentences.t: Sie schliefen aber dreihundert Jahre, bis in der Nacht, worin der Weltheiland geboren ward.
sentences.l: They slept, however, three hundred years, until the night in which the Saviour of the World was born.
sentences.i: But they slept three hundred years, until the night in which the Saviour of the World was born.
sentences.n: “Weltheiland” — Saviour of the world, a compound of Welt + Heiland. “worin” = wherein, in which (a fused relative, common in devotional and legal registers). “ward” again = wurde.

sentences.t: Da erwachten sie und waren mit ihm auf Erden und wurden die zwölf Apostel genannt.
sentences.l: Then they awoke and were with him on earth, and were called the twelve apostles.
sentences.n: The legend closes by naming them: the twelve sleepers rise as the twelve apostles of the Gospels. “genannt werden” — to be called, passive of nennen.

glossary.erhalten: erhalten — to sustain, keep, maintain (infinitive; 'am Leben erhalten' = keep alive; 'sich aufrecht erhalten' = keep oneself upright)
